subject: Geo handshake: SLA window, temporary egress acceptance criteria & subprocessor onboarding plan
messages:
From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@covenanthealth.ai>

Cc: Covenant Health Legal <legal@covenanthealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary egress / subprocessor onboarding — acceptance criteria and timeline

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare the DPA addendum request for our security board, two quick asks we need to lock down before we take this to procurement:

1) Temporary egress window — acceptance criteria: we need a clear definition of the maximum transient egress window (hours), which regions may be used for transient processing, and a fallback policy if the pinned region is unavailable.

2) Subprocessor onboarding schedule — we require a 30-day notice of any new subprocessor and a roster for the next 90 days (names + roles + country).

3) Proof points — can you provide an example evidence package (ops runbook snippet, audit log sample) that shows how transient egress is logged and how customers are notified?

We’ve attached our internal egress requirements doc for context (Covenant_egress_requirements.pdf). Please loop in the ops and legal folks who can confirm timelines — we’d like to have draft language ready for our SOC/compliance review the week of Aug 2.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Lim
Head of Data Governance, Covenant Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary egress / subprocessor onboarding — acceptance criteria and timeline

Hi Rachel — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps: 

- Transient egress window: we offer a configurable window up to 72 hours for emergency cross-region processing with audit logging; default pinning keeps data in the customer-selected region and transient hops are limited to our vetted failover endpoints.

- Regions used: by default we restrict transient processing to the same geographic cluster (e.g., EU cluster); cross-cluster hops (EU <-> US) are only used under capacity/failover and require explicit customer acceptance.

- Fallback policy: if the pinned region is unavailable we will route to the nearest compatible model variant in the same cluster; if none available, routing will fail closed unless you enable transient egress.

- Subprocessor notice: we can commit to 30-day notice for newly engaged subprocessors. We can provide a 90-day projected roster as requested.

I’ve attached a short SLA matrix and a proposed DPA addendum we typically send as a follow-up (proposed_sla_matrix.pdf). I’m looping in Markus (legal) and Karthik (ops/infra) to add technical and contractual detail.

Next steps: Markus/Karthik — can you confirm the evidence package we can share (audit sample + runbook snippet) and whether we’re comfortable with a 72-hour temporary egress cap as an option? Rachel — once we align on language we can produce a DocuSign addendum for signature.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary egress / subprocessor onboarding — acceptance criteria and timeline

Hi all — quick legal/ops note.

On the evidence package: we can provide an anonymized audit log export and a redacted runbook snippet that demonstrates transient egress handling and notification. I’ve asked ops to prepare a sample (redwood_transient_egress_audit_sample.txt).

On the SLA and acceptance: committing to a configurable 72-hour transient egress window as an opt-in in the DPA addendum is acceptable from a legal perspective, with the following consumer-facing controls:
  - Admin toggle to opt into transient egress for a specified service scope
  - Notification webhook to a customer endpoint when transient egress occurs
  - Post-incident report within 48 hours if transient egress was used outside normal maintenance windows

Subprocessor timeline: we will provide 30-day notice for newly engaged subprocessors; for immediate transparency I’m attaching our current near-term roster export. Any subprocessors added within the next 90 days will be shared in a roster CSV and are subject to our standard contractual flow.

Requested action: Rachel — are you OK with the DocuSign flow (link below) and signing timeline? We’d like approval to publish the addendum so procurement can review before your SOC meeting.

Regards,
Markus
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference

Rachel — following up on Markus’ note with a couple of operational clarifications from Karthik: 

- Encryption keys: customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, keys are region-bound; a transient hop will not export plaintext to another KMS — keys remain within the region cluster and we use envelope encryption when moving tokens.

- Notification webhook: we can configure a test webhook to send a sample transient-egress event to a Covenant endpoint; Grace is available to coordinate the endpoint format and replayed test events.

- DocuSign: Markus’ team will publish the DPA addendum draft; once you confirm language we’ll issue a DocuSign for signature. Suggested internal acceptance window: sign by Aug 5 to meet your SOC review date.

I’ve included the prior emails below for context.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Marissa

Marissa — thanks to you, Markus and Karthik for the clear answers. A few clarifications before we sign: 

1) The 72-hour cap is acceptable as an opt-in, provided we get the webhook notification and post-incident report commitments in writing.

2) For encryption keys: Covenant’s preference is that key material never leaves the EU KMS. Can you confirm whether envelope encryption and the region-bound KMS model sufficiently meet that requirement for hosted customers? If you can provide a short technical note (one page) confirming key material residency semantics during transient hops that would satisfy our architecture review.

3) We’ve reviewed the subprocessor roster — thanks. We’ll route the addendum to procurement for an Aug 5 internal deadline. Please send the DocuSign when you have the final addendum.

If you can get the technical note and the redacted audit sample by Thurs (Jul 29) we can keep to our timeline.

Appreciate it —
Rachel
Head of Data Governance, Covenant Health
